name: Gridlock and deadlock handling
maintainer: Synthesised from SUMO documentation (DLR / Eclipse SUMO) and the sumo-user mailing list
first_release: N/A (teleporting has been part of SUMO for many releases; exact introduction year not verified) [uncertain]
last_activity: SUMO 1.28.0 (2026-10-08) ChangeLog still lists deadlock fixes (sublane deadlocks, meso time-to-teleport at stop edges); 1.27.1 fixed a deadlock on junctions with parallel internal lanes
code_availability: N/A (lesson; mechanisms are in the open-source SUMO code at https://github.com/eclipse-sumo/sumo)
known_limitations: WHY JUNCTIONS LOCK UP. In microsimulation, a deadlock is a cycle of vehicles each waiting on the next. SUMO classifies stuck vehicles as: 'wrong lane' (no connection from the current lane to the next route edge, with 'highway' as the fast-road case), 'yield' (on a minor road with no gap in priority traffic), 'jam' (on a priority road with no space on the next edge), 'blocked' (behind a stopped vehicle), 'disconnected' (no permitted connection for the vClass), 'bidi' (oncoming traffic on a bidirectional lane) and 'railSignal'. Root causes are usually network errors, not driver behaviour: mis-modelled right-of-way, missing or wrong connections, junction clusters from OSM divided roads (short internal edges), keepClear=false connections, unsuitable signal plans, and demand above capacity with spillback into upstream junctions. POLICIES AVAILABLE IN SUMO. (1) Teleport: a vehicle first in line and below 0.1 m/s for --time-to-teleport (default 300 s; 0 or negative disables) is removed and moved along its route at average edge speed until space appears. Time at scheduled stops does not count. Variants: --time-to-teleport.highways (wrong lane on roads faster than 69 km/h, default 0 = off), .disconnected, .bidi, .railsignal-deadlock, .remove (delete instead of reinsert), --max-num-teleports (abort if exceeded, default -1). (2) Junction-blocker ignore: --ignore-junction-blocker <s> (default -1 = never) lets vehicles ignore foes that have stood inside the junction for that long, modelling drivers squeezing around. Note: no vType attribute literally named 'jmIgnoreJunctionBlocker' exists in current SUMO docs. The per-vType equivalents are jmIgnoreKeepClearTime (default -1), jmIgnoreFoeProb/jmIgnoreFoeSpeed, jmIgnoreJunctionFoeProb, and impatience (0 to 1, growing over --time-to-impatience, default 180 s). (3) Keep-clear (no-block) heuristic: on by default (--default.junctions.keep-clear true), so vehicles do not enter a junction unless they can leave it. It can be disabled per node or connection, which is a known cause of deadlocks. (4) Roundabout priority: netconvert --roundabouts.guess (default true; structures over 3500 m circumference excluded) gives circulating edges right of way over entering edges, which balances inflow and outflow. If guessing fails (for example when a cycle path crosses the ring), entering vehicles get priority and the ring locks. The fix is an explicit <roundabout edges=.../> in plain XML, or a priority junction type with raised edge priority inside the ring. Signalised roundabouts can still deadlock from downstream spillback or bad plans. (5) Insertion control: --max-depart-delay (default -1) drops vehicles that cannot enter; departLane=best avoids wrong-lane insertion. (6) Collisions: --collision.action defaults to teleport (none, warn, teleport, remove). LIMITATIONS OF THESE POLICIES. Teleports conserve vehicles but corrupt travel times, delay and queue metrics. Teleporting vehicles are invisible and absent from FCD output, so a visualisation silently 'loses' cars. --ignore-junction-blocker does not clear jams caused by wrong-lane vehicles unless their waiting time exceeds the threshold. Lowering time-to-teleport hides network errors rather than fixing them
documented_failures: (a) Roundabout not recognised because a bicycle path crossed it, so priority went to entering vehicles and the roundabout deadlocked (sumo-user). (b) An OSM-imported signalised roundabout where each node was its own traffic light kept collapsing; joining the signals under one controller did not stop it (sumo-user). (c) Networks with many keepClear=false connections produced a different kind of junction deadlock (sumo-user). (d) OSM divided roads without --junctions.join give clusters of short edges that cause throughput loss, jams and deadlocks (SUMO OSM import docs). (e) A user found --ignore-junction-blocker did not clear a jam caused by a wrong-lane vehicle; the maintainer said this was expected behaviour (sumo-user). (f) SUMO itself still fixes engine-level deadlocks: parallel internal lanes (1.27.1) and the sublane model (1.28.0, Git main), which is relevant because Indian scenarios will run the sublane model
validation_approach: SUMO emits a warning for every teleport with vehicle, lane, time and reason. Teleport counts appear in summary output ('teleports', due to jamming or collisions) and in meanData. Practitioners locate the hotspots in sumo-gui at the reported time and lane, fix the network or signal plan, and rerun until teleports approach zero. --max-num-teleports can act as a hard fail gate in automated runs
takeaway_for_our_build: Treat gridlock as a first-class, user-visible result, not an engine detail. Concretely: (1) keep SUMO's teleport on (300 s default) so runs always finish, but parse teleport warnings and summary output and show teleport count, reason and location on the map as a 'scenario health' panel; flag any run where teleports exceed about 1% of trips as unreliable, and exclude teleported trips from delay statistics or mark them. (2) Run a pre-flight network check after every user edit: netconvert with --junctions.join, --roundabouts.guess and --lefthand; reject or warn on disconnected edges and on removed keepClear. Re-emit explicit <roundabout> definitions for rings the user draws. (3) Use departLane=best and a finite --max-depart-delay so insertion backlogs are reported, not hidden. (4) Expose --ignore-junction-blocker (for example 30-60 s) and vType impatience as an 'Indian assertiveness' preset, since Indian drivers do squeeze past blockers, but label it as a behavioural assumption. (5) Cap wall-clock and step count per run, and set --max-num-teleports as a circuit breaker so a locked scenario fails fast instead of burning server time. (6) Pin a SUMO version of 1.28.0 or later, given the recent sublane deadlock fixes
